gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-hind-madurai: Cultural and classic, Edo SZ draws lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals. Hind Madurai does the quieter job, with s curves open at both ends, while the heading handles the statement-making.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-khula: Khula brings a tall midsection and curves that hold their mouths open beneath Edo SZ, whose lowercase has cast iron stature. That unwavering stroke width in the heading is the standout.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-matangi: Sturdy all the way down, with twine-like strokes underneath. Edo SZ is best at monumental, constant-stroke headings, while Matangi does its best work as a hefty, open-rounded lowercase body.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-mozilla-text: Cast iron up top, tall flared lettering below. Edo SZ earns its keep when big and brief, its constant pen pressure unmistakable, while Mozilla Text carries bold-looking lowercase with outward-flaring terminals.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-nata-sans: Contemporary, clean Nata Sans follows a heading with cast iron presence. Edo SZ lays down one constant stroke width, and the sans below lets wide, unclosed curves breathe in a large central band.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans: Cast iron stature meets an open, easygoing lowercase. Noto Sans fills most of the letter height with lowercase and keeps a wide c, so paragraphs keep moving after Edo SZ makes its stand.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Wire-like strokes up top, tall full letters below. Edo SZ is best at holding one thick line through every letter, while Noto Sans Armenian is best at inviting round shapes and tall c, s and z.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Cultural weight sits up top, where Edo SZ gives its lowercase the stature of cast iron capitals. And Noto Sans Balinese, with room inside every curve and short ascenders, lets paragraphs unspool without a snag.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Noto Sans Cherokee stands tall, with short stalks above. Its e leaves a wide gap at the terminal, so text flows smoothly beneath Edo SZ, whose every stroke ends at one measured thickness.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-chorasmia: Noto Sans Chorasmian reads large and open, with short ascenders. Give Edo SZ, with its drawn-wire weight, plenty of size and it will hold its ground against the sans-serif text below.
